name: Aspect-Category-Detection
description: Aspect-Category-Detection is a restaurant review dataset where the model must identify which predefined aspect categories (AMBIENCE, DRINKS, FOOD, LOCATION, RESTAURANT, SERVICE) are discussed in a given review text.
card_text: This dataset contains 200 text samples of restaurant reviews paired with instructions to detect aspect categories. Each sample provides a raw review text as context and a prompt asking which categories from a fixed list (AMBIENCE, DRINKS, FOOD, LOCATION, RESTAURANT, SERVICE) are discussed. The target output is one or more category labels, making it a multi-label classification task. Reviews vary in length from very short phrases to a few sentences and reflect subjective dining experiences. The dataset evaluates a model's ability to infer fine-grained aspects beyond overall sentiment, relying on a closed category set defined by the prompt.

context.semantics: The raw text of a restaurant review, providing the main content to be analyzed for aspect categories. It typically contains the reviewer's personal experience, opinions, or brief comments about a dining establishment.

question.semantics: An instruction prompt that asks the model to identify which aspect categories are discussed in the review and lists the allowed categories (AMBIENCE, DRINKS, FOOD, LOCATION, RESTAURANT, SERVICE).

category.semantics: The target aspect category label or labels assigned to the review, chosen from the predefined set. Multiple labels may be present as a comma-separated string when several aspects apply.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of a raw restaurant review context, an instruction-style question asking which aspect categories are discussed, and an output category field containing the applicable aspect label(s) from a fixed set. The context supplies the text to analyze, the question defines the classification task and allowed categories, and the category field gives the target answer.
